2028 Mercedes-AMG GT 63 Is the Monster Rival SUVs Have Bad Dreams About
63 photos
Photo: Mercedes-AMG
As a sort of general, unspoken rule, carmakers don’t usually come out with information, details, and photos of new car models over the weekend. Yet, this Saturday, that’s exactly what German carmaker Mercedes-AMG did, as it pulled the wraps off the second vehicle it built on the AMG.EA architecture.
Following in the footsteps of the AMG GT 4‑Door Coupe, the newcomer is called the 2028 Mercedes-AMG GT SUV, and it makes no secret of what it is all about: a full-size SUV powered by an electric drivetrain, meant to offer, in the same package, the performance levels usually associated with AMG and the practicality of a vehicle in this class.
The GT is not just any other SUV, but the first one to have been specifically developed from the ground up in-house by the high-performance brand. It’s also the first Mercedes to come with the AMG Active Ride Control+ system that throws into the mix active pitch and roll stabilization to contribute to a smoother ride.
We’ve already covered the basics of what the newcomer family brings to the world of performance SUVs, and we’ll go through that again later in the story. Until then, though, I think it’s worth having a look at the model that’ll spearhead the range, the AMG GT 63 SUV.
This model is the most potent of the lineup of three SUV versions that will be sold as part of this family, at least as it shapes up to be for now – the other two being the entry-level Mercedes‑AMG GT 53 SUV and the Mercedes‑AMG GT 55 SUV.
Photo: Mercedes-AMG As specced for the American market, the 63 is, just like its siblings, built on a 119.7-inch wheelbase and measures a little over 200 inches long, almost 80 inches wide, and a tad over 65 inches tall. Despite these dimensions and its rather bulky appearance, it comes with a drag coefficient of 0.27, which is about the same as the Hyundai Ioniq 9 and the Toyota Prius.
That matters, as the easier this thing cuts through the air that opposes its forward motion, the more drivers can squeeze out of its electric powertrain. And the numbers provided by Mercedes are impressive even on paper.
The AMG GT 63 SUV is animated by a trio of axial flux motors that deliver a peak output of 1,153 hp and 1,475 lb-ft of torque. When it comes to continuous output, though, horsepower levels drop to 711.
That’s still enough to get the beast, which tips the scales at 5,941 pounds (2,695 kg, curb weight), to an electronically limited top speed of 168 mph (270 kph), and allows it to accelerate from zero to 60 mph in just 2.6 seconds.
Photo: Mercedes-AMG The three electric motors are only one of the two major components the SUV relies on to become a nightmare for the competition. The other one is the battery pack, a 128-kWh Formula 1-based 800-volt piece of hardware with directly cooled cylindrical cells, which is good for a maximum range of 435 miles (700 km, as measured under WLTP).
The pack supports a 710-kW DC charging capacity, and that translates into 280 miles (450 km) of range being gained in just ten minutes of being plugged in. That also means the state of charge can get from ten to 80 percent in just 12 minutes.
The 2028 Mercedes-AMG GT 63 packs all the latest technologies developed by Mercedes-AMG, including an Aerokinetics roof spoiler and air panel designed to reduce aerodynamic drag, and a number of seven drive programs, including one that replicates the sound of a V8 engine for those who might miss such a thing,
Mercedes will release the AMG GT 63 SUV onto the American market in the summer of next year, and that means pricing for it hasn’t been announced yet. The same happens for the two other models in the range.
Photo: Mercedes-AMG As a reminder, the mid-range AMG GT 55 SUV is equipped with the same electric powertrain as the 63, but offers lower numbers in terms of performance: 805 peak horsepower (711 hp continuous) and 1,372 lb-ft of torque. Because it uses the same battery pack as its higher-spec sibling, range stays the same.
The entry-level AMG GT 53 SUV relies on a completely different powertrain, consisting of a 106-kWh battery and two permanently excited synchronous electric motors. The motors crank out a combined 536 hp peak and 362 hp continuous, while maximum range stands at 415 miles (668 km).
The 2028 Mercedes-AMG GT 63 will not have it easy going up against the likes of the Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric or the Lucid Air Gravity GT-S, but neither will these rival electric SUVs. The arrival of the new AMG beast is likely to energize the market in the coming years as the battle for supremacy in this segment heats up.
We’ll keep an eye on AMG and report back when pricing for these three newcomers is announced. Until then, one more thing: Mercedes will offer no less than 60 exclusive Manufaktur colors for the SUV, along with AMG wheels that can be enhanced with new color accents for the first time.
